original_question: Determine whether the qualitative structure of generic inhomogeneous spacelike singularities is stable when one includes the matter fields expected in the early universe, rather than restricting to vacuum or highly simplified matter models.
target_in_paper: Section 5.2, Problem P16: "Determine the structural stability of generic inhomogeneous spacelike singularities for general matter fields present in the early universe." ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s target as a question about generic inhomogeneous spacelike singularities and about whether their asymptotic behavior remains stable once one includes realistic early-universe matter, rather than staying in vacuum or overly simplified matter settings. That is exactly the theme of the discussion immediately leading to Problem P16. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))

refined_question: Within general relativity, for a generic inhomogeneous cosmology approaching a past spacelike singularity, determine whether the asymptotic singularity structure is structurally stable when one replaces the previously studied vacuum or simplified matter settings by the general matter fields relevant to the early universe, especially matter of the kinds singled out nearby in the paper such as massless scalar and electromagnetic fields. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))
justification: This is the correct target because Section 5.2 first sets the BKL-style singularity context, then separates neighboring problems about locality (P14) and spikes (P15), and only after that states the matter-stability problem as P16. So the draft is aiming at P16, not at the locality or spike problems. The paper does not provide an explicit equivalent reformulation of P16; the sentences after it add heuristic context through cosmological billiards and related matter/supergravity systems, rather than proving equivalence.
